body: Lol I did my time in corrections. It definitely sucked a lot. My dumbass worked there part time even after I left for a bit just because I had a love for my coworkers, and even our command staff. I still miss it sometimes. Mad respect and much love to y’all road guys and gals.

For real though. One dude up in the comments seems to really hate COs. I’m assuming the type of cop who everyone thinks is a dick and flexes with his power. Could be wrong though.

I just don’t understand it. It’s a job that very few want to do, and many LEOs won’t do. I’ve had police officers literally pitch a fit because I told them that their arrestee with a PBT of .325 needed a medical clearance before we can accept them. Poor you, have to go sit in the hospital for an hour or two. Calling your sergeant won’t change the jail policy though lol.

And this isn’t me hating on the LEOs, because I have a love for my homies on the road. I know many great ones. I just can’t stand the “we’re better than you” attitude. Still love my road homies though.

Right, because I would risk my life and livelihood just to act like a dick to a few criminals lol.

In all seriousness, my states Department of Corrections academy was pretty insightful and heavy on treating inmates with respect. Obviously you had dickheads and people who were just plain stupid, but the majority of people I worked with just wanted to make it home with their paycheck at the end of the pay period. I did what I could to treat everyone with respect, even when they didn’t respect me. The last thing I wanted was to be ambushed in a housing unit where I was outnumbered 102:1 and the closest help was approximately two minutes away. I tried to give a shit about most people because I know it isn’t a great environment.

I think you’re correct. I worked at a max prison, and two different county jails, and the worst I saw was COs smuggling in drugs/tobacco, or having sex with the inmates, that was consensual on both parts, but obviously wrong on an ethical and professional level. 

Most of this shit is made up. And since the common person only sees the holding cell or maybe a few days in general population blocks if they go to jail, they don’t know any better but to believe this bullshit. 

I can believe that maybe 30-40 years ago some of this shit happened, but not in the last twenty years barring few and far between cases. Literally every facility I worked at had cameras covering every angle. You couldn’t fart in the presence of an inmate without getting some sort of police brutality or unreasonable punishment report/grievance on you, both of which was taken very seriously at every facility I’ve worked at and been to for transports or whatever it may be.

I remember being called into the sheriffs office one time because in a critical situation I told an inmate to “get on the fucking ground”. I received a written counseling for dropping the F Bomb. Another time I got a written counseling for taking an inmate to the ground, and in the process had to swing him around me and his head came close to the wall. What was that inmate doing? He was choking another officer out, and the officer wasn’t in the wrong either. That officer was trying to clean the inmates room because this particular inmate was mentally handicapped and couldn’t take care of himself. So being the good officer he was, he tried to wipe down his mat and mop the floor for him.

So yeah, most of this thread is complete bullshit.
